dominant_strengths: SF Pro typography is precisely set with confident hierarchy between the giant 'iPhone' wordmark and quieter nav.
Product tile row demonstrates exceptional craft: consistent silhouette scale, neutral backgrounds, and disciplined label spacing.
Native Apple system feels inevitable — global nav, promo strip, and grid behave exactly as the ecosystem trains users to expect.
dominant_weaknesses: Layout is template-locked; the lineup row reads as a CMS grid rather than an editorially composed hero moment.
Massive 'iPhone' wordmark floats in dead whitespace with no supporting tagline or imagery, weakening emotional payoff.
Innovation is near-zero — visually identical to a decade of prior Apple product index pages, no fresh system gesture.
fix_priorities: Pair the 'iPhone' wordmark with a hero device shot or motion sequence to convert empty space into visceral impact.
Differentiate the 'New' iPhone 17e tile with a stronger visual cue beyond a text label to reward scanning.
Introduce subtle scroll-driven motion or parallax in the lineup tiles to elevate the reflective layer.
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral clarity dominates; visceral impact is muted by empty hero space and reflective distinctiveness is low because it mirrors every prior Apple index.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — it functions correctly as an iPhone product index, but it is a competent execution of an existing pattern rather than a designed solution.
